chapter: Bandleaders and talent on the boats
title: Calliope playing, and the afternoon calliope concerts in St. Louis
summary: The calliope's loud sound and 28 keys, and the afternoon concert from the 4,500-passenger boat in St. Louis.

blocks.x: He was on the boat. He was on the boat. He was on the boat. He was on the boat. What about Steve Lewis? When was he on the boat? I don't remember Steve Lewis. He was supposed to play the Kalanke here. I think in his... Put a raincoat on or something. Walk out of that water. Maybe they all did. Well, they could. But they always put cotton in the rear. They did that. Because it was pretty loud. You see, if you could play it louder. Except for the one of the steam pressure, they have a rain.

If you wanted to carry a great distance and made it hard for the panel player to play it. That's why then you give them a little more an early. They foul. But very few people don't play the Clack. So you only have 28 keys. And everything has to be. Because now, the piano first, the first, We have a five-pound boat in St. Louis now in the afternoon. We play for the entertainer, the people in the afternoon. It's a big thing. And it happens with the piano player. It's an A1 piano player. He can call on right quick. In fact, we've had a five-pound number eight years. He took it off on the other boats in the afternoon. And he plays it in the afternoon. And the night fellow plays it at night, but the man at night is not nearly so good. But in the afternoon, he goes on a concert. It's really worthwhile. The boat carries 4,500 people. And everybody that can get on that top deck goes up there to listen to that five music. And those kids go home and talk about it until next year. And they want to go back to that five. It's something they never hear. Any other place like that. It's close to it and I don't see how it's done. Did you hear it in St. Louis?
No, I wish I had known about it.

Did you go on the Admiral? No, I was up there. I was up there. I was up to the band just for two weeks. And I was out of part of February and first part of January. What were you last year?
